question: Why do heavily reshared meme images turn blotchy even when nobody edits them?
answer: Because every save throws a little more away. JPEG compression splits a picture into 8-by-8 pixel blocks and discards detail the eye tends to miss; each screenshot or re-upload repeats the cut, and errors pile up as blocky edges and smeared colour. The grain on an old reaction image is its travel record.
move: A copy of a copy keeps the losses of every copy before it.
reference: ITU-T Recommendation T.81, Digital compression and coding of continuous-tone still images, International Telecommunication Union, 1992
